$comment: v2.3 plan 03. Every place in src/runtime and src/wizard that writes AFTER an await, and what has been done about it. Generated set, hand-classified status. The guard in src/runtime/ownership.guard.test.ts fails when this file and the code disagree, in EITHER direction: a new site nobody classified, a row whose site is gone, a "checked" row with no token check in its body, or a "todo" row that has quietly acquired one (flip it to checked). Statuses: checked (verifies a RunToken before writing) | delegate (awaits a censused site that owns the check) | local (writes nothing that outlives the call) | todo (owed work). WHAT "checked" MEANS, PRECISELY: the body contains a token check -- NOT that every write is preceded by one. The detector is a body-level scan, so it cannot see the interleaving, and a body that gains a fifth host step can escape the checks that guard the other four (found 2026-09-22 in EffectsApplier.applyCheckpoint: the preset sat below the Author Note await and the background below applyCastChanges per-member awaits). Per-write checking is proven by TESTS in the case files (effectsOwnership.review.test.ts pins each check with a case that reaches it), which is also the file-level rule: a check without a case is a check a mutation can delete.

src/runtime/effectHost.ts#restoreEffectT.note: PARTIAL: one inverse per effect target, and the GUARD IS THE CALLER. `EffectsApplier.restoreEffects` reads each target's current value and compares it with what this chat wrote before calling anything here, and refuses the ones that no longer hold it — so a restore that outlived its chat cannot overwrite an edit someone else made. The token would add the chat-switch case, which the leave/rollback/restart callers own; each branch here is a single stHost seam whose own result is returned as the answer.

src/runtime/effectsApplier.ts#EffectsApp.note: PARTIAL: guarded entirely from its CALLER. Its own body has no await before the write, so a guard inside would mint at the moment of the write and prove nothing; commitBoundary checks ownsOpenChat before calling it. Any new caller must do the same.

Checked before EVERY host-facing write rather than once per group of them (2026-09-22: the preset sat below the Author Note await and the background below applyCastChanges per-member awaits with no check between, so the background was the one write that could land in another chat; it now checks per member inside the loop, before the preset, and before the background). It stops rather than completing, because whatever moved the world runs its own applyCheckpoint.

v2.3 plan 03: the only effect that SPEAKS — fireReply posts a message into whatever chat is open, so a late fire is visible in the transcript. One await per reply, so the check is inside the loop. Limit: beginRun mints at entry, so it detects the world moving DURING the sequence, not before; the caller owns that decision. Live-proven 2026-09-20: plan02-runtime scenario green twice against a group with the required cast, npcFired=1 — the guard does not suppress a real scripted reply. The trigger (generating) branch is still unproven live.

Before anything is written back, the host's current value is read and compared with what this chat wrote; a target that no longer holds it is refused and marked externally-changed rather than overwritten. What the token would add is the chat-switch case, and the caller owns that decision: `restoreEffects` runs from the leave/restart/rollback path, which re-reads the world it is leaving, and every host write it performs is delegated to the injected `restore` (a stHost seam).

src/runtime/loreSelect.ts#LoreSelector.f.note: v2.3 plan 11 §Fault matrix: split out of select() so a refused force is reported instead of discarded, and so the token check sits where the write is. Both callers (the fresh path and the cached re-force) minted the run and pass it in, so the cached path — which had NO token check at all before this — is covered too. The story swap that the cached path could not see is fixed in the CACHE KEY, not here: a token minted at the start of a call can never notice that a cache entry was built under a story the chat has since left.

src/runtime/memoryMirror.ts#syncMemoryMi.note: v2.3 plan 03: it already had a hand-rolled chat comparison guarding the binding, which the census could not see and which only asked about the chat. A story swap inside the same chat passed it, and the mirror book is per-chat but shared across stories. The comparison is kept (it is the only guard an unwired host has) and the token check added beside it.

src/runtime/rollback.ts#runRollback.note: v2.3 plan 04. The rollback composition, extracted from the manager for its line budget. Partial, not checked: it verifies no token of its own, because it does not start any work — it is the mutation's own consequence. `rollbackFromMessage` records the mutation position on the owner before calling it, the run it composes belongs to the chat the runtime is loaded for, and every host write it triggers (world-info re-apply, stagecraft revert) is one this census already covers at its own edge. Making it `checked` means minting a token inside work that the mutation just invalidated, which would refuse the rollback it exists to perform.

src/runtime/storyUpdate.ts#applyStoryUpd.note: v2.3 plan 03: mints before the unbounded author popup and refuses keep, restart and cancel side effects when the world changes before the choice returns. Successful restart and swap own their later epoch-changing writes separately.

src/runtime/talkControl.ts#TalkControlle.note: v2.3 plan 03: mints against the director window before the judge/director call, captures the origin checkpoint and message id, refuses to cache or record a decision whose world moved, and re-checks a cached or in-flight entry so a stale one cannot serve a world that replaced it. Exact pending identity keeps an old task from clearing its replacement. The returned guard also gates the two host effects the callers perform (abort, triggerMember) and the audit row now names the world the decision was computed from. No journal record on discard: the host has no journal seam here, and extras.talk.decisions renders every row as a chosen speaker or a silence, so a discard row would read as a silence.

src/runtime/turnBridge.ts#TurnBridge.flu.note: v2.3 plan 03, V4 2026-09-23: the single pending slot is now a queue (a group round used to collapse into one boundary). Each entry keeps the guard captured when its reply was accepted; lapsed entries are dropped before polling, and each is re-checked immediately before its own commitBoundary. Only entries whose after-speak finished (ready) are committed, in order from the head, so an older reply never commits a newer one early. Controls in turnBridgeOwnership.review.test.ts + turnBridgeIdentity.review.test.ts.

src/runtime/turnBridge.ts#TurnBridge.onR.note: v2.3 plan 03: captures ownership at event acceptance, queues its own pending entry (V4: no longer replaces a shared slot), and refuses a late afterSpeak continuation after its world lapses by removing its entry. The flush retains the same captured guard rather than minting in the landing world.

src/runtime/memoryQueue.ts#commitDecisio.note: v2.3 plan 05. Owns the write for all four author decisions (resolve, dismiss, Store anyway, reconfirm), which is why their own rows are gone: each now returns a call to this one instead of writing below its own await. COVERED: the put-back runs only on evidence of a lost write (a request that never went out, a non-2xx, or a read-back showing an older boundary), it writes only this runtime own memory slice, and the one host-facing write awaits MemoryCoordinator.save, which awaits RuntimeManager.persist, where the chat check lives. NOT COVERED: no run token of its own -- and it cannot mint one, because the row it resolves is named by the AUTHOR rather than read from a window, so there is no span to mint against (the same reason the four decision rows were delegates) -- and the restore names arrays snapshotted BEFORE the save, so a memory write landing inside that window is clobbered. An id-keyed restore is recorded as a v2.4 seed rather than hidden here.
